title: Pilot Failure Mode Playbook (ops + seller cheats)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, seller-friendly + ops-ready playbook for pilot activations that go sideways. Target audience: platform sellers, SEs, customer success leads, and on-call infra/ops. The goal is to give rapid decisions and customer-safe language so pilots can be stabilized or safely paused with minimal churn.

Scope:
- Short, actionable failure-mode cards (symptom -> immediate seller line -> ops triage -> mitigation -> customer comms)
- Lightweight runbook checklist for pilot kickoff and emergency pause
- Postmortem prompts and success metrics to move from reactive -> proactive

How to use this doc:
- Sellers keep a copy on the pilot onboarding ticket.
- If an incident is suspected, use the "Seller Triage" lines verbatim until ops confirms a cause.
- Ops run the triage checklist and pick a mitigation.
- Update the ticket with the chosen mitigation and customer-facing note.

Failure Mode Cards:
1) Latency Spike (sudden API P50/P95 jump during pilot)
- Indicators: P95 > promised SLA by >3x; tokenizer/streaming stalls; customers report timeouts for >5% of calls
- Seller immediate line: "We're seeing higher-than-expected response times on a small percentage of requests; we're investigating and will apply a temporary routing change to keep your integration responsive."
- Ops triage checklist:
  * Confirm metrics in Console route dashboard (token latency, queue depth, worker CPU/GPU).
  * Check recent deployment/rollout events (canary starts, model swap).
  * Inspect batching/queue backlog and autoscale events.
- Quick mitigations (choose one):
  * Route pilot to lower-latency model variant (pin to same family but smaller size).
  * Lower max_seq/window to reduce per-request work; enable prefix caching if applicable.
  * Flip to dedicated reserved pool or temporary burst capacity if signed contract allows.
- Rollback/stop criteria: latency normalizes to within 1.5x SLA for 30m.
- Customer-facing note template: "We routed your pilot to a lower-latency variant to keep responses snappy while we diagnose. There may be minor quality differences; we'll follow up with a summary and timeline."

2) Model Regression (quality drop / hallucination spike)
- Indicators: increased low-score responses in eval harness; customer flags >3 bad responses per 1000; divergence from golden prompts
- Seller immediate line: "We're seeing a handful of responses that don't meet our expected quality. We've paused the model roll and are investigating a safe fallback to maintain correctness."
- Ops triage checklist:
  * Check recent model version rollouts and config changes.
  * Run golden prompt suite in sandbox against current and previous versions.
  * Confirm tokenizer/sequence trimming or prompt truncation isn't the cause.
- Quick mitigations:
  * Roll back to previously pinned model version for the pilot.
  * Enable strict fallback to an earlier verified model family for the affected routes.
  * Throttle/limit tokens for suspect prompt shapes and open a follow-up to refine prompt engineering.
- Rollback/stop criteria: golden prompt pass rate returns to baseline within 1 hour.
- Customer-facing note template: "We've temporarily reverted the pilot to a verified model version to ensure output quality while we investigate. No action required on your end."

3) Capacity Eviction / Preemption (GPU pool contention)
- Indicators: worker evictions, queue spike + 503s, autoscaler throttles, spot/interrupt notices
- Seller immediate line: "We're seeing a capacity interruption affecting a small set of pilot requests. We'll route around the impacted machines and update you shortly."
- Ops triage checklist:
  * Check pool health and eviction logs.
  * Verify autoscaler events and reserve capacity metrics.
  * Validate fallback routing policy (region/instance type) is operational.
- Quick mitigations:
  * Route pilot to alternate capacity tier (dedicated vs burst) or different region.
  * Enable lower-throughput mode (reduce concurrency) to preserve correctness.
  * If on private, coordinate with customer infra to unlock more nodes.
- Rollback/stop criteria: 503 rate < 0.1% for 20 minutes.
- Customer-facing note template: "Some backend capacity was interrupted; we've re-routed your pilot to maintain availability. We'll share root cause and timeline after our analysis."

4) Authentication / IAM Errors (token or key misconfig)
- Indicators: 401/403 spike, recent API key rotation, permission errors in audit logs
- Seller immediate line: "We're investigating an access mismatch that is preventing a small portion of pilot calls from succeeding. Could you confirm no key rotation occurred on your side in the last hour?"
- Ops triage checklist:
  * Inspect token issuer logs, KMS access events, and service account mapping.
  * Check client SDK versions for known auth bugs and proxy layers for header stripping.
- Quick mitigations:
  * Re-issue short-lived test key and validate with customer in-situ.
  * Route pilot through the former control plane for compatibility while we debug auth config.
- Rollback/stop criteria: auth error rate < baseline and all test tokens succeed.
- Customer-facing note template: "We're seeing an auth mismatch in a subset of requests. We have a short test key ready if you'd like to validate quickly; otherwise we'll coordinate a safe update window."

5) Data Leakage Suspicion (sensitive output or PII leakage)
- Indicators: customer flags containing PII, anomaly detector alerts for sensitive tokens in outputs, eval fails on red-team prompts
- Seller immediate line: "We take data safety seriously. We've paused the pilot for the affected routes while we validate whether any outputs included sensitive data."
- Ops triage checklist:
  * Pull recent outputs for the pilot and run automated PII detectors.
  * Confirm prompt sourcing and any prompt-augmented context for accidental inclusion.
  * Escalate to security/compliance for legal guidance.
- Quick mitigations:
  * Pause the route and switch to read-only test mode (no logging of responses).
  * Re-run outputs through post-generation scrubbing temporarily.
  * Engage Customer Success + Security to prepare a disclosure if leakage confirmed.
- Rollback/stop criteria: zero confirmed leakage and security sign-off.
- Customer-facing note template: "We've suspended the affected route as a precaution while we verify outputs for sensitive content. We'll share findings and remediation steps as soon as possible."

Cold-Start / Cache Miss (prefix/KV cache cold)
- Indicators: sudden step change in latency for recent prompt shapes; warm cache metrics show <5% hit rate
- Seller immediate line: "We're seeing a cold-cache effect on some newly exercised prompts. Performance should stabilize as the system warms up; we'll actively prime caches for your common flows."
- Ops triage checklist:
  * Check cache hit-rate dashboards and recent prompt histograms.
  * Apply manual cache priming for critical prompt sets if possible.
- Quick mitigations:
  * Prime KV/prefix caches with a curated set of common prompt flows.
  * Temporarily pin to a version with better cold-start characteristics.
- Customer-facing note template: "A small portion of requests is slower while the service warms up. We expect steady performance within the next X minutes and are priming caches now."

Emergency Pause Runbook (one-page checklist)
- When to pause: data leakage suspected, repeated quality regressions, sustained SLA breach >30m, or repeated 5xx >1% across pilot calls.
- Steps for seller:
  1) Copy and paste the approved customer-facing note for the failure mode.
  2) Flag the pilot ticket and @ops-oncall in Slack with the header: "PILOT PAUSE: <customer> <short reason>".
  3) Move to 'paused' state in Pilot Tracker spreadsheet and list next follow-ups.
- Steps for ops/oncall:
  1) Confirm the triage checklist for the relevant failure card.
  2) Execute immediate mitigation (route swap, rollback, pause).
  3) Post an initial incident note: short cause hypothesis, mitigation taken, ETA for full update.
  4) If security-related, engage security and legal immediately.

Postmortem prompts (short):
- What triggered the failure? (config, model, infra, customer input)
- What detection signals failed or succeeded? (alerts, dashboards)
- Could the pilot have been prevented by a warm-up, constraints, or a different routing policy?
- Action items (owner + SLA to complete): quick fix, test plan, documentation updates, seller play refresh.

Success metrics to close a pilot incident:
- Customer-facing availability >= agreed SLA for 72 hours after mitigation.
- Regression test pass rate >= baseline on golden set for 24 hours.
- No recurring incidents of same class in 30 days for the pilot.

Templates (copy-paste friendly)
- Immediate customer note (generic): "We're seeing an issue with your pilot integration that affects X% of requests. We've applied a temporary mitigation to protect your experience. We'll send a follow-up summary with next steps within Y hours."
- Pause confirmation: "Pilot is paused for <reason>. We'll coordinate a restart once we've validated the fix. Please expect a diagnostic summary within N hours."

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Should we publish a short FAQ for customers explaining the model-variant tradeoffs for fallbacks? (proposal: 1 pager for legal+sales)
- Define exact SLAs for burst capacity during pilots (ops + finance input needed).
- Automate a 'pilot safe-mode' toggle in Console (engineering backlog item).

Refs / links mentioned:
- Pilot tracker sheet (internal): CONFLUENCE-PLAT-3421
- Runbook skeleton: JIRA-OPS-9782
- Quick test harness PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quick-checks/pr/124

Notes to self: keep this pocket-sized (one A4/slide) for sellers. We should convert to a two-slide cheat deck: 1) failure-mode cards + seller lines, 2) operational checklist + templates.
